description: Purple petals with pale wedged stems, gathered past bloom. Meadow blobs trail them wherever they bounce.
lore: Hold one up against an [[monsters/butterfly_dragon|Emberwing]]'s wing at ten paces — closer is a mistake, and the tellers have the name of the man who tried it — and the banding matches. Violet, then the pink line, then violet again, then the pale wedge at the base where the petal leaves the stem. Not similar. The same, down to where the colour changes.

Which means the wing was copied. Which means that on the other side of all this, on an afternoon nobody wrote down, a person lay on their front in a meadow with their face a hand's width from an iris and looked long enough and hard enough to keep it. They were not thinking about being remembered. They were looking at a flower. Twenty-two gold off any stall on the road, and the closest thing to a picture of one living hour that anyone here will ever hold.
gm_notes: The petal is the evidence that the dragon's wings were borrowed from a real afternoon. Hands players a living-world moment without a single fact about the living world.
